summary.intent: Reframe the documentation and weekly record so that recall against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) is not read as a correctness measure, putting checker-judged wrong shares beside it. The work was delegated to a subagent and the result is tracked as PR #412.
summary.outcome: A subagent pushed commit 161fa76a (signed) on docs/rdt-recall-framing and opened PR #412, linked to trail #259. The assistant rewrote the PR body. CI was still running and the Python script tests had not been confirmed with a proper exit code, so the PR awaits user approval.

repo: Recall against RDT means the share of RDT's reference components and props that Caliper also reports. It is not a measure of correctness.
Checker-judged wrong shares from the 2026-11-06 weekly run: Caliper 0 to 1.09% and RDT 0.006 to 5.02% on props both tools list, across Mantine, Chakra, shadcn, antd and Spectrum.
The 'omits whole files' figures (51 of 295 antd, 265 of 1,240 shadcn) are react-docgen throwing, not RDT omitting files, so docs must not attribute them to RDT.
docs/rdt-differences.md holds the source table of per-corpus figures and the difference classes (9, 16 for non-components, 8 for truncation) that other docs link to.
The repo has no recall chart or image; the only README image is the brand hero in assets/brand/.
The `wrong` figure both over- and under-counts, which measurement.md now states.

Relevant checks: `just lint doc-check machete typos` and the Python unittest modules test_weekly_review, test_weekly and test_headline (72 tests). CI has a Python scripts job and an Entire Gates check that needs user approval.
workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output with no user authority, so the assistant checked the diff and CI status itself before summarizing.
Writing the PR body to a temp file and passing it with `gh pr edit --body-file` avoids shell-quoting problems with long markdown.
A blank exit code from the test run meant the worker judged success by the 'OK' line, so CI's exit-code check remains the authoritative verification.

friction: The exit code printed blank when the Python tests ran, so pass/fail had to be inferred from the 'OK' output.
CI checks on PR #412 were still running, and Entire Gates needs the user's approval, so the PR could not be confirmed green.
The user's earlier mention of a 'chart' matched nothing in the repo, leaving the assistant unsure what was meant.
open_items: Confirm CI's Python scripts job passes on PR #412 and get the Entire Gates approval.
Ask the user where the recall chart lives if it was a rendered image outside the repo, then replace it.
The full Python test suite beyond the three modules was not run.
